author: Rick Fritz
text: All CGMs have a chemical coating on the cannula, the part that is inserted into your skin.  That chemical helps calculate your glucose continuously.  Your body chemistry interacts with the chemical as it dissolves.  If it dissolves faster than the clinical study data, most likely you will not achieve the promised duration of the CGM and/or experience erratic CGM results.  If it dissolves slowly and on a consistent rate, you will experience more stable results for the full duration of the CGM.  Manufacturers use a proprietary chemical on their CGMs along with a proprietary algorithm, which means some people get good results with one brand vs another.  That is why there are some people that swear by Dexcom or Libre because of how the chemical and algorithm interacts with their body chemistry.

author: DeterminedPomelo1502
text:
Dehydration causes the Abbott FreeStyle Libre to produce artificially high glucose readings. Because the sensor measures glucose in the interstitial fluid, low fluid levels reduce the volume of this fluid, causing glucose to become more concentrated. 
This can result in inaccurate, falsely high readings or significant spikes.
